newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. T-bond slightly up in Tokyo, awaits Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. T-bond slightly up in Tokyo, awaits Greenspan.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond were slightly higher in post-holiday Tokyo trade on Tuesday as the dollar's firmer levels kept prices well-supported. Other prices were steady to firmer by late morning trade, traders said.

But operators refrained from taking fresh positions actively before Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony before the Senate later on Tuesday and ahead of the two- and five-year Treasury note auctions this week.
"I'm looking towards Greenspan's testimony as the key factor to determine the next trend. But I don't expect the 30-year yield to move above 7.0 percent," a bank trader said.

In early December, Greenspan's remarks, saying that the Fed must be wary when "irrational exuberance" infects stock and other asset markets because that could end up doing damage to the economy, rocked U.S. stock and bond markets.

"I don't expect to see heavy sales of Treasuries even if Greenspan makes similar comments (as he did last December) as the bond market has gone through further corrections since that time. Prices are already low enough," another trader said.
The key 30-year bond was at 95-28/32, yielding 6.82 percent, against 95-26/32 in New York on Friday. March T-bond futures were up 1/32 at 110-31/32 from the previous close.
